inst_cams_intro: AI Detector finds most IP cameras on your network by itself. Make sure the cameras and the computer are on the same network — preferably with a cable — and that the camera sends out a video stream (RTSP).
inst_cams_reolink: Reolink — RTSP is switched off at the factory, so you have to enable it once. Open the Reolink app, select the camera, tap the gear icon and go to Network → Advanced → Server Settings (or Port Settings). Switch on RTSP and ONVIF and save.
inst_cams_hikvision: Hikvision & Dahua — RTSP and ONVIF are usually enabled by default. You do not have to change anything.
inst_cams_others: Axis, Foscam, Ubiquiti UniFi — also stream RTSP out of the box, on the standard port 554.
inst_cams_rtsp_enable_caption: Example: enabling RTSP in the Reolink app under Network → Advanced → Server Settings.
inst_setup_cams_1: When AI Detector starts, setup opens in your browser by itself. Nothing opens? Go to http://localhost/.
inst_setup_cams_2: Choose your language at the top right: English, Nederlands, Deutsch or Français.
inst_setup_cams_3: The cameras found on your network are already ticked. A camera that needs its own login asks for its username and password.
inst_setup_cams_4: A camera is missing? Click Enter a stream URL instead and paste its RTSP address — use the table below to find it.
inst_setup_cams_5: Check each picture and give every camera a name you recognize, for example Heifers barn 1 or Calving pen.
inst_setup_cams_caption: Setup step 1: every camera that is found shows its picture. Give each one a clear name.
inst_setup_cams_add_caption: Cameras → Add camera: tick the cameras that were found, or enter a stream URL yourself (addresses hidden in this screenshot).
inst_setup_existing: Moving to a new computer? Before you add a camera, choose Use existing setup and select the folder of your previous installation. Cameras, detectors, alerts and recordings are imported; nothing is sent or started.
inst_stream_urls_title: Find the RTSP URL for your camera
inst_stream_urls_note: Replace [PASS] and [IP] with the password and IP address of your own camera. Prefer the Sub stream where available — it is sharp enough for the AI and uses far less processing power.
inst_setup_det_title: Setup 2 of 3 — Choose what to detect
inst_setup_det_intro: A detector watches the cameras you choose, records what it sees and alerts the people you pick. Choose a preset: it supplies the AI model and all settings, and keeps the detector up to date with newer models.
inst_preset_cc: Cow Catcher — heat detection: recognizes mounting behaviour.
inst_preset_calv: Calving Catcher — calving detection: water bag, legs, head and the newborn calf. Also has a Low Power mode for slower computers.
inst_preset_tailup: Calving Catcher Tailup — calving variant that watches for the raised tail.
inst_preset_general: General — a general model, for your own use outside the barn.
inst_setup_det_1: Tick the cameras the detector should watch. A camera can be watched by several detectors — for example Cow Catcher and Calving Catcher on the same pen.
inst_setup_det_2: Phone alerts and the AI check can be added right away or later (see the next steps).
inst_setup_det_3: Want a second detector? After setup, go to Detectors → Add detector and choose another preset.
inst_setup_det_caption: Setup step 2: pick a preset and the cameras it should watch.
inst_setup_start_1: Every camera is checked once. Then click Start monitoring.
inst_setup_start_2: On the first start AI Detector downloads the model and prepares it for your hardware. That can take a few minutes.
inst_setup_start_3: As soon as the cameras are really being analysed, Recordings opens. The green dot at the top left says Monitoring.
inst_setup_start_4: Monitoring keeps running when you close the browser.
inst_setup_start_caption: Setup step 3: each camera is checked, then monitoring starts and keeps running in the background.
inst_tele_intro: Telegram is the fastest free way to get an alert on your phone, including the video clip of the detection. You create your own bot once; it takes about two minutes.
inst_tele_1: Open a detector (or go to Settings → Alerts → Add recipient) and click Connect Telegram.
inst_tele_2: Click Open BotFather, send /newbot and follow the instructions for a name and username.
inst_tele_3: Copy the bot token from BotFather into AI Detector. Keep this token private.
inst_tele_4: Choose where alerts go: My phone, A group or A channel.
inst_tele_5: Scan the QR code with your phone (or click Open Telegram), press Start and confirm the test alert in the chat. Then save the detector.
inst_tele_caption_token: Connect Telegram: create a bot with BotFather and paste its token.
inst_tele_caption_qr: Scan the code with your phone and press Start in Telegram (QR code blurred).
inst_tele_review_title: Confirm or reject from your phone
inst_tele_review_text: Every alert has 👍 and 👎 buttons. Your answer is saved with the recording in AI Detector, so you build up a reviewed archive without opening the computer.
inst_tele_groups_text: One bot can send alerts to different chats: for example a group Heat detection for the farmer and staff, and a group Calving alerts for the night shift. With quiet hours on a recipient, alerts between two times (for example at night) arrive without sound — they still arrive.
inst_ai_intro: With the AI check, a vision language model looks at every clip again before you get an alert. It filters out most false alarms. The preset supplies the question the AI answers.
inst_ai_1: Go to Settings → AI check and click Connect Google Gemini.
inst_ai_2: Click Open Google AI Studio, sign in with a Google account and create or copy an API key.
inst_ai_3: Paste the key in AI Detector and click Connect. The key is tested with a test image first.
inst_ai_4: In each detector you can switch the AI check on or off.
inst_ai_note: Google offers a limited free tier. Clips of detected events are sent to Google to be checked; everything else stays on your computer. Other providers can be set under Advanced → AI connections.
inst_ai_caption: Settings → AI check → Connect Google Gemini: paste your API key from Google AI Studio.
inst_phone_title: Open AI Detector on your phone
inst_phone_intro: You can open the dashboard on every phone, tablet or computer on the same network as the AI computer.
inst_phone_1: On the AI computer, go to Settings → Devices and click Connect a device.
inst_phone_2: Scan the QR code with your phone, or go to http://aidetector.local/ and enter the code. Codes expire after five minutes.
inst_phone_3: A connected browser is remembered for a year. You can remove access again under Settings → Devices.
inst_phone_4: On an iPhone or iPad you can put AI Detector on your home screen; it then opens like an app. Instructions are under Settings → Home screen.
inst_phone_note: The connection inside your network is not encrypted (HTTP). Only use it on a network you trust.
inst_phone_caption: Settings → Devices: connect phones and computers with a one-time code.
inst_storage_text: Every detection is saved as a recording with photo and video clip on your own computer. Settings, models and recordings live outside the program, so they stay when you uninstall or update. Back up this folder now and then:
inst_storage_docker_path: the folder next to the Compose file
inst_support_diag: Something wrong? Go to Settings → Logs and click Download diagnostics. That file contains everything needed for a bug report. Check it for camera addresses before you share it.
inst_support_youtube: YouTube — search for “CowCatcher AI” for video guides and tips.
inst_support_email: E-mail — questions or problems? Mail us directly:
inst_support_community: Facebook / Telegram community — ask your question in our group for quick help and experiences from fellow farmers.
